title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2611.26366v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. However, differences in data availability across physical conditions can yield a long-tailed training distribution, biasing models toward common rules even when evidence supports rare ones. To study this challenge, we introduce TailWorld, which evaluates the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states while independently controlling training imbalance and calibration informativeness. translated_title: 世界模型更倾向于习得的先验而非视觉证据
translated_abstract: 世界模型正被越来越多地用于模拟物理交互，但为每个环境单独训练一个模型限制了可扩展性。跨环境预测需要识别当前的物理规则，而仅凭外观可能无法揭示这一规则。因此，我们研究了视觉校准（visual calibration）问题：利用短视频中物体的运动和交互作为直接证据来推断当前规则，并从不同的初始状态预测该规则下的运动。然而，不同物理条件下数据可用性的差异可能导致长尾的训练分布，使模型偏向常见规则，即使证据支持的是罕见规则。为了研究这一挑战，我们提出了TailWorld，该基准评估示范规则在不同初始状态之间的迁移能力，同时独立控制训练不平衡程度和校准信息量。该基准将模型预测与来自相同预测初始……的两个参考未来进行比较。
tldr: 该论文揭示了世界模型在跨环境预测中倾向于依赖训练数据中的常见规则先验而非视频中的视觉证据，并提出TailWorld基准来独立控制训练不平衡与校准信息量，以评估示范物理规则在不同初始状态间的迁移能力。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that world models favor learned priors of common physical rules over visual evidence from videos, and introduces TailWorld, a benchmark that independently controls training imbalance and calibration informativeness to evaluate the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states.
